root_cause.text: In btusb_work() in the Bluetooth btusb driver, the code used the unbounded active SCO connection count from hci_conn_num() as data->sco_num - 1 to index a fixed three-entry alts[] table, causing an out-of-bounds array access when more than three SCO links were active.
root_cause.evidence: The patch adds `sco_idx = min_t(unsigned int, data->sco_num - 1, ARRAY_SIZE(alts) - 1);` before `new_alts = alts[sco_idx];`, replacing the previous direct lookup `alts[data->sco_num - 1]`, and the CVE/commit explicitly states that the table has only three entries while `data->sco_num` was used directly without constraining it.

intent_record.intent_summary: Clamp the SCO-based `alts` array index to a valid range to prevent out-of-bounds access in `btusb_work`.
intent_record.what: The change adds a new local variable `unsigned int sco_idx`, replaces the direct array access `alts[data->sco_num - 1]` with a bounded index computed by `min_t(unsigned int, data->sco_num - 1, ARRAY_SIZE(alts) - 1)`, and then uses `alts[sco_idx]` instead.
intent_record.how: At runtime, this prevents indexing past the end of the 3-element `alts` array when `data->sco_num` is greater than 3 by clamping the computed index to the last valid element, avoiding out-of-bounds access and selecting a safe fallback alternate setting.

grouping_result.intent: Clamp the SCO-based `alts` array index to a valid range to prevent out-of-bounds access in `btusb_work`.

relevance_review.reason: The change directly addresses the root cause by bounding the SCO-derived index used to access the fixed-size alts[] array in btusb_work, preventing the out-of-bounds access when too many SCO links are active.

candidates.rationale: This directly uses the unbounded SCO connection count minus one as an index into the fixed-size 3-entry alts array, causing out-of-bounds access when more than three SCO links are active.
This defines the fixed three-entry table that is later indexed by data->sco_num - 1 without bounds checking; the mismatch between fixed size and unbounded index is part of the root cause.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs the out-of-bounds-prone access by using the unbounded SCO connection count minus one as an index into the fixed-size three-entry alts array, matching the described root cause.

bic_trace_step.reason: The snippet includes the relevant btusb_work() logic, so it is sufficient to judge. The vulnerable construct is still present in the CVSD path: `static const int alts[3] = { 2, 4, 5 };` followed by `new_alts = alts[data->sco_num - 1];`. This uses `data->sco_num - 1` as an index into a fixed 3-entry array with no bounds check. Since `data->sco_num` is set from `hci_conn_num(hdev, SCO_LINK)` in `btusb_notify()` (`data->sco_num = hci_conn_num(hdev, SCO_LINK);`), the count is effectively unbounded here. If more than three SCO links are active, `alts[data->sco_num - 1]` becomes out-of-bounds, matching the stated root cause. The added logic for transparent audio (`air_mode`, alt 6 support, `btusb_find_altsetting`, `btusb_switch_alt_setting`) does not add any bounds check or clamping for the CVSD `alts[]` indexing, so the fix is not present.
